extracted.intended_audience: general readers, donors, potential partners, and journalists interested in ProPublica's mission and standards
extracted.subtask_description: Organizational principles and quality criteria that guide ProPublica's investigative reporting — what kinds of stories it pursues, how it devotes resources, and the journalistic/organizational commitments it makes. Useful for assessing whether reporting meets ProPublica's stated mission and practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission to expose abuses of power
rubrics_metrics.description: To expose abuses of power and betrayals of the public trust by government, business, and other institutions, using the moral force of investigative journalism to spur reform through the sustained spotlighting of wrongdoing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories should identify and illuminate abuses of power or betrayals of public trust, and be pursued with the explicit goal of prompting reform or accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depth and persistence of reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: We dig deep into important issues, shining a light on abuses of power and betrayals of public trust — and we stick with those issues as long as it takes to hold power to account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accept that investigative journalism requires significant time and resources; reporters should pursue long-term, sustained coverage rather than one-off pieces when needed to achieve accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on stories with potential to spur real-world impact
rubrics_metrics.description: We focus on stories with the potential to spur real-world impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize reporting topics and angles that can lead to tangible changes (e.g., new laws, policy reversals, accountability for leaders). Use potential for public benefit as a selection criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topical scope of coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: With a team of more than 150 dedicated journalists, ProPublica covers a range of topics including government and politics, business, criminal justice, the environment, education, health care, immigration, and technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate proposed projects against these topical domains; cross-cutting topics that affect public trust or reveal institutional failures fit the mission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence and nonprofit funding model
rubrics_metrics.description: ProPublica is an independent, nonprofit newsroom that produces investigative journalism with moral force. As a nonprofit, ProPublica’s work is powered primarily through donations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain editorial independence from funders; funding should primarily support journalistic work rather than shape coverage. The nonprofit model implies accountability to public-interest goals rather than commercial pressures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource allocation to world-class journalism
rubrics_metrics.description: The vast bulk of the money we spend goes directly into world-class, award-winning journalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allocate organizational resources primarily to reporting capacity — experienced reporters, data analysis, legal support — rather than non-journalistic overhead, to ensure investigative quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment to uncovering truth regardless of cost or time
rubrics_metrics.description: We are committed to uncovering the truth, no matter how long it takes or how much it costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects should not be abandoned solely for cost or duration reasons if they are central to the mission of exposing wrongdoing and promoting reform.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparent financial reporting to donors and the public
rubrics_metrics.description: We practice transparent financial reporting so donors know how their dollars are spent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain public transparency about funding sources, expenditures, and how donor money supports investigative work; transparency is part of organizational accountability.
